properties.areaDesc: Beaufort; Pamlico; Southern Craven; East Carteret
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 6:32AM EST until November 26 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along the southern Pamlico Sound, Bay and Lower
Neuse Rivers, Core Sound, and adjacent tidal creeks, and areas
along the Pamlico and Pungo Rivers and adjacent tidal creeks.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in some areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in an elevated threat of property damage. Flooding
will extend inland from the waterfront threatening some homes
and businesses. Isolated road closures and flooding of
vehicles will be possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday
and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to
bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the
week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal
low impacting the area. The higher of the high tide cycles
will be during the morning hours each day this week. This is
forecast to bring nuisance water level rises on Tuesday across
the watch area with minor to locally moderate impacts forecast
on Wednesday. The worst impacts are currently forecast with
the morning high tide cycle on Thursday.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.areaDesc: Ocracoke Island; Hatteras Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 6:32AM EST until November 27 at 10:00AM EST by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 2 to 4 feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Areas along the beaches, Pamlico Sound, and adjacent
tidal creeks, and Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...From Wednesday evening through Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. This includes impacts
to Hwy 12. Low lying property including homes, businesses, and
some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Some shoreline
erosion may occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides will be peaking on Wednesday
and Thursday before gradually lowering which will continue to
bring elevated water levels to the area through much of the
week. The King Tides will be exacerbated by a strong coastal
low impacting the area Wednesday evening into Thursday
morning. The higher of the high tide cycles will be during the
morning hours each day this week. Initially ocean overwash
will be a concern as 10-15 ft seas impact the area beaches.
This will be of greatest concern across the more vulnerable
dunes along Hwy 12. However as winds switch to a SW direction
Thursday afternoon and evening minor water level rises (around
1-2 ft) on soundside locations of Hatteras and Ocracoke Island
will be possible as water sloshes back towards the eastern end
of the Pamlico Sound.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 24 at 4:49AM EST until November 27 at 3:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Two to three feet of inundation above ground level
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Atlantic, Cape May, Atlantic Coastal Cape May, Coastal
Atlantic and Southeastern Burlington.

* WHEN...From Thursday morning through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding may become severe enough to
cause structural damage along with widespread roadway flooding
in coastal and bayside communities, and near inland tidal
waterways. Some locations may become isolated by the flood
waters.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Confidence is high on at least moderate
coastal flooding occurring with Thursday morning's high tide.
Tide levels could potentially reach the major threshold,
especially along the back bays. Stay tuned to the latest
forecast for any changes. Significant beach erosion is
possible. Breaching of sand dunes may occur.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Watch means that conditions favorable for
flooding are expected to develop.

Be prepared to begin taking appropriate action to protect life
and property. Follow the recommendations of local emergency
management officials. Be sure to check the latest forecast from
time to time in case a warning is issued or any new information
becomes available.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 24 at 4:16AM EST until November 26 at 1:00AM EST by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of southeast Florida, including the following
areas, Coastal Broward County, Coastal Miami Dade County, Coastal
Palm Beach County, Metro Broward County, Metro Palm Beach County
and Metropolitan Miami Dade.

* WHEN...From this evening through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The last 30 days of rainfall has been 400 to 600 percent of
normal across portions of Palm Beach and Broward Counties, and
between 200 to 300 percent of normal across portions of
Miami-Dade County. This amount of rainfall has made the ground
very saturated over the east coast metro areas of South Florida,
and thus it will not take much rainfall to create exacerbated
flooding issues across the east coast metro areas.

Most likely amounts: 2-3 inches of rain Reasonable Worst Case
(High-End): 4-6 inches of rain
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 24 at 12:44AM PST until November 27 at 1:00PM PST by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...Orange County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this
morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning
to 1 PM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding will be
around the time of the morning high tide, with peak tides
trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at
7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set
back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday, but a long period west
swell arriving late Wednesday will bring larger surf by
Thursday morning's high tide. Breaking waves may reach 4-6 feet
with local sets up to 7-8 feet on west-facing beaches. Surf
lowers to 3- 5 feet by Friday morning's high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal flooding
expected. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
6- 8 feet, sets up to 10-12 feet along west-facing beaches.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM PST this
morning. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 4 AM this morning
to 1 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 1 PM
Wednesday to 4 AM PST Friday. Most susceptible time of flooding
will be around the time of the morning high tide, with peak
tides trending from 7 AM today to 10 AM on Friday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King tides peak through Wednesday at
7.9-8.3 feet, likely breaking the all-time tidal records set
back in late October. Background surf on top of the tides will
remain around 2-5 feet through Wednesday morning, but a long
period west swell arrives Wednesday afternoon, bringing a sharp
increase to the surf for late Wednesday into Thursday. Breaking
waves may reach 6-8 feet with local sets up to 10 feet on west-
facing beaches. Surf lowers to 5-7 feet by Friday morning's
high tide.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

properties.areaDesc: San Juan and Vicinity; Northeast; North Central; Northwest; Culebra; St.Thomas...St. John.. and Adjacent Islands
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued November 24 at 4:06AM AST until November 25 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE...In Puerto Rico, beaches along the northern coastline,
from Aguadilla to Fajardo, including Culebra. In U.S. Virgin
Islands, northern exposed beaches of St. Thomas, St. John and
adjacent islands.

* WHEN...From noon today through lat tonight.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
properties.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM MST this morning.

* IMPACTS...Low visibility could make driving conditions hazardous.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...In addition to low visibility, freezing fog
can deposit a thin layer of ice on roads, creating slick spots and
treacherous travel, especially over bridges and overpasses.
properties.instruction:
If driving, slow down, use your headlights, and leave plenty of
distance ahead of you.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 24 at 2:40AM EST by NWS Baltimore MD/Washington DC
properties.description:
* TIMING: 11 AM through 4 PM.

* WINDS: North at 10 to 15 mph with gusts up to 20 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY: As low as 25 to 30 percent.

* 10-HOUR FUEL MOISTURE: 10 to 12 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: Upper 40s to low 50s.

* IMPACTS: The combination of low relative humidities and breezy
north winds will lead to an increased risk for the spread of
widfires today.


Residents and visitors are urged to properly dispose of cigarette
butts, matches, and any other flammable items in appropriate
containers. Additionally, exercise caution if operating any
equipment that could create sparks and keep vehicles off of dry
grass. Most dry grasses, dead leaves, and other tree litter could
easily ignite and spread fire quickly.

Lastly, remember to obey local burn bans. For more information about
wildfire danger, burn restrictions, and wildfire prevention and
education, please visit your state forestry or environmental
protection website.

For West Virginia, visit www.wvforestry.com
For Maryland, visit dnr.maryland.gov
For Virginia, visit dof.virginia.gov

properties.areaDesc: Kent; Queen Anne's; Talbot; Caroline
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 24 at 2:15AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
properties.description:
There is an elevated risk for fire spread today across the
Eastern Shore of Maryland today. Minimum relative humidity values
will drop to around 25 to 30 percent this afternoon. This will be
accompanied by temperatures rising generally rising into the low
50s and northerly winds around 10 to 15 mph gusting up to 25 mph.
These conditions could support the rapid spread of any fires that
ignite, which could quickly become difficult to control.
Conditions improve during the evening as the wind diminishes and
the relative humidity increases.

Outdoor burning is strongly discouraged. Be sure to properly
extinguish or dispose of any potential ignition sources, including
smoking materials such as cigarette butts. Use caution while
using any machinery outdoors, such as lawn care equipment, that
could cause sparks to come in contact with the dry ground.

This forecast considers meteorological, fuel, and land conditions
and has been developed in coordination with state fire officials.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Western portions of North and Central Texas.

* WHEN...From 11 PM Tuesday to 9 AM CST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Frost and freeze conditions could kill crops, other
sensitive vegetation and possibly damage unprotected outdoor
plumbing.
properties.instruction:
A Freeze Warning means that the season's first episode of
sub-freezing temperatures are likely to occur. These conditions will
kill sensitive plants, and residents are advised to protect tender
vegetation. Automatic sprinkler systems should also be turned off to
avoid creating ice patches on nearby roads, driveways, and sidewalks.

Take steps now to protect tender plants from the cold.

Make sure outdoor animals have a warm, dry shelter, food, and
unfrozen water.

Protect the 4 Ps from cold temperatures: People, pets, pipes, plants.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Del Norte; Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 9:16PM PST until November 26 at 2:00PM PST by NWS Eureka CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
and moderate surf will cause moderate flooding in low lying
areas along the Redwood and Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of
saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.25 and 8.75
MLLW is expected at the Arena Cove tide gauge. At the Crescent
City tide gauge 9.5 to 10.0 feet MLLW is predicted.

* For the Coastal Flood Watch, High astronomical tides and
breaking waves of 25 to 30 feet are expected on Wednesday may
cause major flooding in low lying areas along the Redwood and
Mendocino Coast. Up to two feet of foot of saltwater
inundation above ground level is possible in low lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte, Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal
Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 9 AM to 1 PM PST
Tuesday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday morning
through Thursday afternoon at high tide. Saltwater inundation
will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

* IMPACTS...Several coastal roads may be closed. Low lying
property and some critical infrastructure will be inundated.
These impacts will include, but not limited to highway 101 near
Crescent City and Hwy 1 in low lying areas along the Mendocino
coast. Shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Larger surf is expected to bring more
significant impacts on Wednesday.
properties.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Warning means that flooding is occurring or
imminent. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

Feet Above Ground is locally defined as feet above the Highest
Astronomical Tide or HAT.

* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, High astronomical tides
will cause major flooding in low lying areas mainly around
Humboldt Bay. Up to 3 of saltwater inundation above ground level

waterways. Between 10.3 and 11.0 feet MLLW at the North Spit

saltwater inundation above ground level is possible in low lying
areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.

through Thursday afternoon. High tide is at 11:09 AM on

Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2
hours before and after high tide.

near the Mad River Slough. Shoreline erosion will occur.

highly likely. These conditions will kill crops and other sensitive
vegetation.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 23 at 10:17PM CST by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
Periods of on-and-off light wintry precipitation will continue
across the South Plains, Rolling Plains, and far southern Texas
Panhandle overnight. Initially, precipitation will be a mix of
sleet, rain, and snow, which is then expected to transition to
mostly or all snow early Tuesday morning. Sleet and snow
accumulations, if any, are expected to remain very light with
temperatures near or only slightly below freezing. However, a few
slick spots cannot be ruled out on area roadways, particularly on
bridges and overpasses. Motorists are encouraged to use extra
caution during the morning commute Tuesday. Precipitation will
then come to an end by early Tuesday afternoon.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 7:33PM PST until November 26 at 7:00PM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Higher than normal astronomical tides, the King Tides,
combined with storm surge from large surf and breaking wave
heights of 23 to 28 ft, are expected to bring up to 3.3 ft of
inundation above ground level Tuesday and Wednesday, with up to
2.8 ft of inundation expected on Thursday.

* WHERE...Beaches and low lying areas along the shore lines of
Douglas, Coos and Curry Counties. This includes the
communities of North Bend, Charleston, Port Orford, Gold
Beach, and Coos Bay. Coastal flooding is expected to impact
portions of Highway 101 around Gold Beach, Coos Bay, and
Reedsport.

* WHEN...From 7 AM Tuesday to 7 PM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The worst conditions are expected to be
during the high tide periods in the late morning/early
afternoon. Storm activity lessens on Thursday, but King Tides
will still be present, which will likely continue inundation
impacts. At the Charleston, OR tide gauge, high tide is
expected to be at 10:09 AM today, at 10:51 AM Tuesday, at
11:35 AM Wednesday, and at 12:23 PM Thursday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 23 at 4:02PM HST until November 25 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
...HIGH SURF WARNING IN EFFECT FOR NORTH AND WEST FACING SHORES
OF NIIHAU KAUAI OAHU MOLOKAI BIG ISLAND AND EAST FACING SHORES OF
OAHU...

.A large to extra large, long-period north- northwest swell build
down the island chain on Tuesday. While the source low aimed its
peak swell energy northeast of the area, enough was aimed at
Hawaii to see surf build to warning levels during the day on
Tuesday before subsiding on Wednesday ahead of an even larger
north-northwest swell on Wednesday night into Thursday.

* WHAT...Surf heights of 20 to 30 feet along north-facing shores,
12 to 16 feet along west-facing shores, and 8 to 12 feet along
Oahu's east-facing shores.

* WHERE...North and west facing shores of Niihau, Kauai, Oahu,
Molokai, Maui and the Big Island and east facing shores of Oahu.

* WHEN...From 6 AM Tuesday to 6 AM HST Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...High. Expect very strong breaking waves and powerful
currents. Waves breaking in channel entrances may make
navigating the channels dangerous.
properties.instruction:
Stay away from the shoreline along the affected coasts. Be
prepared for road closures. Postpone entering or leaving channels
affected by the high surf until the surf subsides.

properties.areaDesc: Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 4:04PM PST until November 26 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor to moderate
coastal flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking
waves of 6 to 11 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the
Coastal Flood Watch, significant coastal flooding possible.

* WHERE...Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 8 AM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 6 AM Wednesday to
9 PM PST Thursday. For the Coastal Flood Watch, from Wednesday
morning through Thursday morning.

* IMPACTS...There is a moderate risk for damaging flooding of
sea water over some vulnerable low-lying coastal areas,
especially around the time of high tide, including over
beaches (especially from Santa Monica to Palos Verdes and
Malibu), roads, and structures. Significant beach erosion is
possible. There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Extremely high
tides may cause dock damage and seawater spillage over low
lying areas inside of harbor areas (such as Naples in Long
Beach).

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Extremely high tides of 8.1-8.4 feet will
likely peak between 7am and 11am. An upgrade to a Coastal
Flood Warning would likely come by Tuesday. Coastal Flood and
High Surf Advisories are likely to follow the expiration of
the respective warnings if they are issued.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Plan
for extra travel time as some roads may be closed.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

infrastructure.

expected. Sea forecasts represent an average of the highest
one-third of the combined wind wave and swell height.

midnight. Seas 11 to 19 ft. Rain.

.TUE NIGHT...NE wind 15 to 30 kt diminishing to up to 20 kt after

.WED...N wind 10 to 25 kt. Seas 11 to 14 ft.
.WED NIGHT...N wind 10 to 20 kt. Seas 10 to 13 ft.
.THU THROUGH SAT...S wind 20 kt. Seas 6 to 9 ft.

properties.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Watch issued November 23 at 1:42PM PST until November 26 at 5:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding expected. Inundation of 2.5 to 3.5 feet above ground
level is possible Tuesday along shorelines and low- lying
coastal areas. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves
along the coast. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding possible Wednesday with inundation up to 2.5 to
3.5 feet. For the second Coastal Flood Watch, significant
coastal flooding possible Thursday with inundation up to 2.5 to
3.5 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 8 AM to 3 PM PST
Tuesday. For the High Surf Advisory, from 10 AM Tuesday to 4
PM PST Wednesday. For the first Coastal Flood Watch, from late
Tuesday night through Wednesday afternoon. For the second
Coastal Flood Watch, from late Wednesday night through
Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant coastal flooding due to high tides and
storm surge is expected. This is expected to lead to numerous
road closures. Low lying property including homes, businesses,
and some critical infrastructure may be inundated. Shoreline
erosion or damage may occur. Large breaking waves can knock
people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over
rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while
observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is
expected.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Inundation above ground level refers to the height above the Mean
Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Valleys; San Francisco Bay Shoreline
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Warning issued November 23 at 1:10PM PST until November 26 at 4:00PM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding with up to 2.7 feet of
inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas
near shorelines and tidal waterways.

* WHERE...San Francisco and San Pablo Bay Shorelines.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM PST Monday.
For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM PST
Thursday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW)
at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49
AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:

travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

properties.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 23 at 1:10PM PST until November 26 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, Significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level
is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large
breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...San Francisco County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM Monday to 4 PM
PST Thursday. For the High Surf Warning, from midnight Tuesday
night to midnight PST Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tide gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.4 ft above normal (8.2 ft MLLW)
at 10:05 AM Tuesday, 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at 10:49
AM Wednesday, and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at 11:38 AM
Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of surge that
will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High
tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific
Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.

properties.areaDesc: Central Siskiyou County
properties.headline: Wind Advisory issued November 23 at 12:41PM PST until November 24 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Medford OR
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Wind Advisory, south winds 20 to 35 mph with gusts
up to 55 mph expected. For the High Wind Warning, south winds 30 to
45 mph with gusts up to 65 mph expected.

* WHERE...Most of the Shasta Valley in central Siskiyou County. This
includes portions of Interstate 5 as well as the communities of
Weed, Gazelle, Grenada and Montague.

* WHEN...For the Wind Advisory, until 4 AM PST Tuesday. For the High
Wind Warning, from 4 AM to 10 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Damaging winds could blow down trees, power lines, and
unsecured objects. Power outages are possible. Travel could be
difficult, especially for high profile vehicles.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways and roads running west to east,
including highway 97, will be exposed to tough driving conditions
given the strong southerly wind speeds. Winds are expected to be
strongest late Tuesday morning through Tuesday afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

People are urged to secure loose objects, including large or
inflatable holiday decorations that could be blown around or damaged
by the wind.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued November 23 at 1:10PM MST until November 30 at 3:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by an upstream dam release is expected.

* WHERE...Central Yuma County in southwestern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 300 PM MST Monday Nov 30.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is expected. Low-water crossings are
likely to become inundated with water and may not be passable.

an upstream dam release from Painted Rock Dam has reached
Dateland. Flooding is expected along the Gila River within the
warned area.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Farmlands and low-water crossings along the Gila River.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 23 at 10:18AM PST until November 29 at 4:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A series of storms will bring roughly 3 to 6 inches of rainfall
to the southern slopes of the Olympics through Thursday with snow
levels rising to around 5000 to 5500 feet on Tuesday, and as high
as 6000 to 6500 feet on Wednesday. The combination of heavy rain
and relatively high snow levels is expected to push the Skokomish
River near Potlach above flood stage by midweek.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

11/25, and 2.5 ft above normal (7.4 ft MLLW) at 1:51 PM Thu
11/26.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 23 at 1:38AM CST by NWS Lubbock TX
properties.description:
An approaching storm system late Monday will bring increasing
moisture and colder temperatures to the region. Overnight lows are
expected to fall below freezing area-wide, allowing for isolated
to scattered snow showers to develop overnight and continue into
Tuesday morning. Any accumulations are expected to remain light,
with little to no impacts anticipated. However, a few slick spots
cannot be ruled out, particularly on bridges and overpasses.
Motorists are encouraged to use caution during the morning
commute Tuesday.
